item.title: MCP Postgres Server Tutorial: Safe Read-Only Database Access for AI Agents (2026)
item.description:
Introduction

Letting an AI agent touch your database is the fastest way to make it useful and the fastest way to lose data. One hallucinated UPDATE without a WHERE clause is all it takes. This tutorial shows the setup that earns both: an AI assistant that can explore schemas, run analytical queries, and explain slow query plans against PostgreSQL, while two independent layers stop it from writing anything. You will install the actively maintained Postgres MCP Pro server, create a least-privilege read-only database role, and lock the server into restricted mode. It is written for developers who already know what an MCP server is; if you do not, start with our Model Context Protocol pillar guide first.

item.title: n8n Postgres Tutorial: Connect, Query, and Automate (2026)
item.description:
Introduction

Sooner or later every serious n8n workflow outgrows in-memory data. You want orders stored where a crash cannot lose them, a customer table your whole team can query, or an audit log that survives a workflow rewrite. PostgreSQL is the natural home for that data, and n8n ships a first-class Postgres node for talking to it. This tutorial walks you from an empty database to a working workflow that creates tables, inserts rows, reads them back, updates them, and runs parameterized queries safely. It is written for automation builders who know their way around an n8n canvas but have never wired it to a real database, and every step was verified against n8n 2.40.7 and the node’s published parameter names.

item.title: n8n Docker Compose Setup: Self-Hosting with Postgres and Queue Mode (2026)
item.description:
Introduction

Docker Compose is the way n8n’s own team ships production deployments, and it is the only install path n8n guarantees going forward. This guide builds a complete, production-ready docker-compose.yml for n8n: Postgres as the database, named volumes for data, a .env file for secrets, optional queue mode with Redis workers for heavier workloads, and a safe upgrade routine. It works on any host with Docker, from a $6 VPS to a homelab box. If you need the full VPS walkthrough with a domain and HTTPS in front of this setup, read our guide to installing n8n on an Ubuntu VPS first, it ends exactly where this article begins.

item.title: How to Install n8n on Ubuntu VPS (2026): Docker Compose, Postgres & Free HTTPS
item.description:
Introduction

Self-hosting n8n on a cheap Ubuntu VPS is the single biggest cost lever in workflow automation: the same agent workloads that cost hundreds per month on per-operation platforms run for the price of a $6 VPS. This guide walks you through the production-ready setup, Docker Compose, Postgres 18, and free HTTPS via Caddy, on Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04. Every command below is real, the compose file follows n8n’s official hosting examples, and the n8n behavior notes come from actually running n8n 2.40.7 locally.
